overview: Based on the published agenda, the D.C. Everest Area School District Board of Education was scheduled to hold a regular meeting covering the 2026-2027 school year opening, staff employment changes, health insurance renewal, facility study information, and Act 89 implementation. The meeting included reports from district leadership, a student representative, and legislative network updates, along with consideration of professional development initiatives and community engagement projects.

discussions.body: The board was scheduled to review and approve certified staff employment changes for the 2026-2027 school year. Two employment change documents were provided, with the most recent update dated September 15, 2026, indicating ongoing staffing adjustments.

Dr. Casey Nye was scheduled to present multiple items including a welcome to the 2026-2027 school year, School Board Appreciation Week (October 5-11), district updates, Act 89 implementation, Bright Spots National Cohort participation, facility study information, GTCC programming, and a social media class action suit matter. The Executive Assistant was also expected to provide an update.
Assistant Superintendent Jeff Lindell was scheduled to present an update on the Odyssey and Idea program transition, with an attachment detailing the transition plan dated September 11, 2026.

Principal Ted Aleckson was scheduled to present on community engagement efforts, specifically highlighting a Raptor mural project at Rothschild school. This item was expected to showcase positive community partnerships and student engagement initiatives.

The board was expected to review and consider the health insurance renewal for 2027. Two documents were provided detailing the renewal information and the Alternative Health Plan (AHP) renewal for district employees.

The Talent and Culture department was scheduled to present a comprehensive hiring report for September 2026, providing an overview of recruitment and staffing activities during the summer and early school year period.

Dr. Lindell and Dr. Raether were scheduled to present information on summer professional development activities, detailing training and development opportunities provided to staff during the 2026 summer period.

The board was expected to commit to attendance at the State Education Convention scheduled for January 19-22, with the request needed in October to meet early registration and hotel room reservation deadlines in November.

publicComment: A public comment period was included on this agenda as a designated agenda item.
actionItems: Board was expected to approve the agenda
Board was expected to approve minutes from August 19 and September 11, 2026
Board was expected to approve certified staff employment, resignations, and contract adjustments for 2026-2027
Board was expected to approve consent agenda items including Treasurer's Report, Balance Sheet, Budget Transfers, Budget Revisions, Grant Applications, Fundraising Requests, and Science Model gifts
Board was expected to review and approve health insurance renewal for 2027
Board was expected to approve the agenda for the Annual Meeting/Budget Hearing
Board was expected to commit to attendance at the State Education Convention and authorize hotel room reservations
Board was expected to consider and take action regarding seclusion and restraint matters in closed session
title: Regular School Board Meeting - 2026-09-16
